second_order: making Bill and other Gravity Falls marks
theme_note: These codes hold together because people place, propose, locate, or take credit for visible Gravity Falls marks. What varies is the mark—Bill, a pine tree, zodiac, joaje, or the subreddit name—and whether the turn starts, joins, or reports the work.
regrouped_from: Split from an initial making-and-defending group because adding marks and keeping existing pixels intact are different practices.

theme_note: These codes hold together because participants keep an existing Bill intact against erasure, alteration, or the Void. They vary from one-pixel upkeep and eye repair to warnings, restraint, and urgent defence calls.
regrouped_from: Split from an initial making-and-defending group because maintenance answers threats to an existing mark rather than creating one.

second_order: doing the room's April Fools joking
theme_note: These codes hold together because subreddit participants tease, dupe, warn, or play along with April Fools inside the room. The jokes range from a fake Season 3 announcement to general suspicion; none is about the canvas.

These codes hold together because people turn an idea into a workable design by asking how, scaling it down or up, and choosing what version or missing feature to use. What varies is whether feasibility, ambition, or appearance is at issue.

second_order: negotiating space and keeping the peace
theme_note: These codes hold together because people explain borders, request truces, respect neighbours, halt expansion, accept corrections, and offer reciprocal help. What varies is the neighbour and whether the exchange prevents overlap, repairs a misunderstanding, or establishes coexistence.
regrouped_from: Expanded after review to include the pxls.space triangle misunderstanding because it uses the same explaining-and-backing-off practice as the original-canvas truces.

theme_note: These codes hold together because participants direct coordination away from the subreddit into Discord or use Discord to rally builders. They vary between an early invitation for the original canvas and later coordination after the build moved to clones.
This single code calls the room to retaliate against r/NuclearThrone's challenge; it belongs with no other practice because later replies reject rather than extend that call.
regrouped_from: Kept as a single-code theme after separating the initial attack call from replies that ask the two fandoms to coexist.

second_order: mourning Bill and promising to rebuild
theme_note: These codes hold together because people name Bill's loss, say RIP, ask whether he recovered, or promise that he will return. What varies is whether the loss is unfolding, recalled after the canvas closes, or turned immediately into a rebuild pledge.
regrouped_from: Split from rebuilding elsewhere because mourning and promising precede the concrete move to another canvas.

theme_note: These codes hold together because participants continue the project after r/place by starting, joining, crediting, or publicising Bill on PlaceTwo and pxls.space. What varies is the clone, the degree of completion, and whether the turn recruits help or reports work done.
regrouped_from: Split from mourning-and-rebuilding because these codes show concrete work on named replacement canvases rather than only loss or intention.

theme_note: This single surviving title congratulates the room on its Bill, while the deleted image leaves whether the canvas is meant uncertain.
